An explosive cocktail of dogfights, epic music and a gripping story. Out on Steam November 10, 2026. Dawn Aerowar is an interactive animated film. It blends 3D animation, 2D art and full voice acting to tell the story of a fighter pilot on his final mission, driven by revenge against the Empire that took everything from him. Press Play and you are in the War Room: a war map of the whole operation, twelve missions along one route. The next sortie is marked. You launch it from the map. Then the episode plays in full, without interruption. He escorts a weapon no one should know exists. All that stands in his way are the aces of the Saal'Runa Empire, the last pilots standing after years of war. The film runs nearly two hours, mixing aerial combat and drama. Dawn is a story made and composed by veterans of the genre: a man on a mission, and what it would take to stop him. In a world scarred by years of war, the Free Nations stand on the brink of annihilation. With an iron fist, the Saal'Runa Empire has crushed every resistance but one. One pilot flies one last sortie across the whole Empire: the northern front, the strait, the Aegis Sea, the Capital. Patrols chase him and missiles fan out over the clouds. Every flight is staged and animated in 3D, then framed like a film. Faces, hands and cockpits are all hand drawn. Zodiac 1 lost everything to the Empire: his family, his home, his purpose. All he has left is one burning drive: revenge. Along the way, Zodiac will face many enemies, in the air, at sea and on land. But three of them are especially formidable: the three Aces of the Empire. Reaper , the Name of Death, loves war more than peace. Freya , the Imperial Goddess, quotes philosophers in the middle of a dogfight. Miracle , the Guardian Angel, is known for the lives she saved rather than the ones she took. Each of them asks Zodiac the same thing: do you even know what you're fighting for? Zodiac flies alone. The war reaches him only through the cockpit radio, from an AWACS operator he has never heard before. She is talkative, sharp and strangely well informed. A professional voice cast : Sam Hughes, Kira Buckland, Lara Sawalha, Blythe Melin, Sandra Espinoza, Mark Mullens, Jeremiah Foltz, and over thirty additional voices. Every word and every emotion is performed. The soundtrack is fully original and composed to picture : orchestral, fast-paced and epic, with choirs, Bulgarian voices and classical guitar, plus two original songs. Written by Jose Pavli, the composer of Project Wingman, it runs 77 minutes. Dawn runs in its own app, with subtitles and Steam achievements. The film has 12 episodes and runs nearly two hours. Subtitles are available in English, French, Italian, German, Spanish, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Russian and Brazilian Portuguese. The film was 186% funded on Kickstarter by more than 600 backers. A map lets you follow the progress of Zodiac's mission. After each episode, you can open a dossier with information on the places and characters you have encountered. This War Room expands the lore and helps you understand the story in more detail, in case anything slipped past you. If you prefer, Cinema mode lets you watch the film in one sitting: the 12 episodes play back to back without interruption, and you can return to the War Room afterwards. input.china_demand: Build and lead a colony on the surface of an endless Wall. Manage resources and your people, develop new technologies, defend against relentless zyrex attacks, and send robo-spiders on risky expeditions. Keep the colony from collapsing – in Wall World, it's easy to fall. The Wall is a colossal structure stretching far beyond the visible horizon, hiding traces of ancient eras and unexplained phenomena within its depths. Here, among stone, metal, and darkness, humanity has been forced to build a new life – clinging to the Wall and trying to survive in a world full of threats and mysteries. Wall World Strategy is a colony sim on a sheer vertical surface, where every decision affects the stability of the system. Build and expand your base, gather resources, take care of your people, strengthen your defenses, and send expeditions into distant regions and unexplored depths. Each new step forward brings not only opportunities for growth but also new dangers. Survival depends on your foresight, your ability to manage limited resources, and your willingness to make difficult decisions. BUILD AND EXPAND THE COLONY Establish a base on the surface of the Endless Wall and gradually turn a small outpost into a large, stable, and well-defended colony. Plan the placement of key structures, develop production chains, expand living areas, and build infrastructure capable of supporting both population growth and stable operations. As your colony grows, you will need to decide how to expand, which structures to prioritize, and where to allocate resources – whether into production, housing, or defense. WITHSTAND THE THREATS The Wall is far from lifeless. In its shadows lurk zyrexes – dangerous creatures that will attack your colony again and again, testing its defenses, organization, and your ability to respond. Strengthen your defenses, secure vulnerable areas, and decide how much you can afford to invest in protection. Step back into 1980s–90s China and play Dou Di Zhu, Guandan, Sichuan Mahjong, Ka Wu Xing, and more in 3D hometown scenes lit by your own clock. Practice against AI and rewind any move. Buy once, no ads. Welcome to Chinese Board & Card Games Museum Step back with us into the streets and courtyards of 1980s and 1990s China, where regional card and mahjong tables from across the country are gathered into one playable museum. Across China, the same deck of cards or set of mahjong tiles takes on different rules, names, and rhythms from one city to the next. Here, clear rulesets, cultural exhibits, and smooth tabletop matches live side by side. There is no required reading before you play—feel free to look around, sit down to a game you grew up with, or read an exhibit label and discover a game from another region. Every way to play has a hometown Inside the museum, we have recreated the local setting where each game grew up. Pull up a chair at any table, and you step right into the daily life of that city: Head to a Wuhan alley on a summer night to play Dou Di Zhu in the evening breeze; Visit a canal-side home in Huai'an for a partnership round of Guandan; Climb to an autumn rooftop in Changsha and race to empty your hand in Pao De Kuai; Step inside a Xiaogan main hall in winter to play Ka Wu Xing behind closed doors; Sit down in an early-spring Chengdu teahouse to play Sichuan Mahjong to the last tile; Or stay right by the Eight-Immortals table in the center of our museum hall for a game of Sheng Ji, played all across China. The lighting in these old streets follows your computer’s clock—lamps come on at dusk, and a midnight game means midnight outside the window too. Clear skies, rain, snow, or fog: you choose. Take a breather and the camera wanders the city for you. Prefer to focus purely on the cards? Switch to Simple Mode anytime to skip the 3D scenes and go straight to the table. Misplayed? Play it again Every move against the AI is recorded. Step back to any move, play it differently, and the game branches from there. The original line is kept, so you can switch back and compare at any time. Available in all six games. Branching sessions are for practice and do not count toward your match record. A quiet table We want to give you a quiet place to play. Buy once: no ads, no top-ups, nothing nudging you along. Guandan and Sheng Ji also include guided lessons, and Sheng Ji comes with a built-in card tracker. More exhibits on the way The free demo currently offers six games—Dou Di Zhu, Guandan, Pao De Kuai, Sheng Ji, Sichuan Mahjong, and Ka Wu Xing—all supporting Steam friend rooms (in testing). Early Access is planned for Q4 2026 and will continue to welcome more regional games beyond these six, with the initial lineup announced at launch. Every game has a history Beside every table is an exhibit story and a lineage tree. Every branch on the tree cites its historical source; where accounts disagree, we draw the line dashed. Each table also states the exact ruleset adopted in the museum. House rules vary wildly from town to town—if yours differ, come tell us in the discussions. Local rules are the collection this museum treasures most. A growing museum Yandra Studio is building this museum piece by piece. More regional games and rulesets will keep arriving, and each one is placed on display only once it plays smoothly and its story can be told properly. Available on Windows with mouse and keyboard controls. No controller support yet. Switch between Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English in the game without restarting your match. Traditional Chinese uses Chinese audio.
